info.text: Interactive check questions for Lesson 8.1: Constructing Positive and Negative Apparatus by Hand.

name.text: 01 Question: The Function of the Apparatus Criticus

questiontext.text: In digital scholarly editing, what fundamental ontological shift does the critical apparatus undergo relative to traditional print editions?

generalfeedback.text: The critical apparatus is not an ornamental footnote but a structured data model recording evidence of historical transmission.

answer.text: It ceases to be a static typographical footnote and becomes a machine-actionable data model of historical textual transmission.

feedback.text: Correct. Digital apparatuses model textual variation as an intrinsic, computable graph of historical transmission rather than compressed page footnotes.

answer.text: It is replaced by automated spell-checking algorithms that eliminate the need to record scribal variation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Textual criticism records variation as historical evidence; digital editing enriches rather than eliminates apparatus records.

answer.text: It serves exclusively as a graphic visual display without underlying machine-readable markup.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The core transformation is precisely that the digital apparatus becomes structured, machine-actionable XML data.

answer.text: It merges all historical manuscript variants into a single standardized text without recording witness differences.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The apparatus exists specifically to document differences across witnesses, preserving the evidence of transmission.

name.text: 02 Question: Positive vs. Negative Apparatus in Print Tradition

questiontext.text: What distinguishes a positive critical apparatus from a negative critical apparatus in classical print philology?

generalfeedback.text: A positive apparatus explicitly attests every witness for both lemma and variants, whereas a negative apparatus records only deviating witnesses to economize space.

answer.text: A positive apparatus explicitly lists witness support for both the lemma and all variant readings, whereas a negative apparatus explicitly lists only diverging witnesses.

feedback.text: Correct. In a positive apparatus, support for the lemma is affirmatively declared (e.g. 'λόγος] A B ; νόμος C'), while a negative apparatus omits lemma witnesses to save print space (e.g. 'νόμος C').

answer.text: A positive apparatus records only authentic readings, while a negative apparatus records only scribal errors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. 'Positive' and 'negative' refer to whether witness attestation for the lemma is explicitly printed or left implicit, not to editorial value judgements.

answer.text: A positive apparatus is encoded in TEI XML, whereas a negative apparatus is generated automatically by CollateX.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Both terms originate in print philology centuries before digital markup and computational collation existed.

answer.text: A positive apparatus evaluates grammar, whereas a negative apparatus evaluates paleographical script.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The distinction relates strictly to explicit versus implicit witness attestation for the lemma.

name.text: 03 Question: The Epistemological Danger of the Negative Apparatus

questiontext.text: Why does the negative apparatus pose a severe epistemological danger when ingested by computational stemmatology algorithms?

generalfeedback.text: Silent agreement in a negative apparatus conflates witness presence with physical absence, introducing fatal errors into automated stemmatic analysis.

answer.text: It relies on silence to imply agreement, causing algorithms to falsely score physically damaged, missing, or uncollated witnesses as agreeing with the lemma.

feedback.text: Correct. In a negative apparatus, silence is interpreted as assent. Algorithms reading omitted witnesses generate false positives for the base reading, distorting statistical distance.

answer.text: It uses overly verbose XML markup that causes computational parsers to run out of memory.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Negative apparatuses are compressed and terse; the problem is ambiguous silence, not XML verbosity.

answer.text: It prevents human readers from understanding the linguistic meaning of the accepted lemma.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The danger is algorithmic and evidentiary: conflating physical absence (lacunae) with active witness agreement.

answer.text: It forces editors to use Latin abbreviations that modern character encodings cannot represent.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unicode can represent all Latin abbreviations; the flaw is the unrecorded status of damaged or omitted manuscripts.

name.text: 04 Question: The TEI P5 Critical Apparatus Module (textcrit)

questiontext.text: What is the primary function of the TEI P5 textcrit module (Chapter 13)?

generalfeedback.text: The TEI P5 textcrit module provides a standardized XML vocabulary that converts textual variation from static print footnotes into machine-actionable data.

answer.text: To provide a standardized, interoperable XML vocabulary that encodes complex multi-witness textual variation as structured, machine-actionable data.

feedback.text: Correct. The textcrit module provides dedicated elements like , , , and to model textual variation independently of proprietary software.

answer.text: To automatically correct Greek and Latin spelling errors in digitized transcriptions without human oversight.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The textcrit module provides markup structures for representing variation, not automatic text correction.

answer.text: To convert scanned manuscript images directly into searchable PDF documents.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Optical character recognition and image handling belong to other tools and modules, not textcrit.

answer.text: To restrict digital editions to traditional negative print footnotes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The module is specifically designed to overcome print limitations by supporting rich, multi-tiered positive apparatus architectures.

name.text: 05 Question: Core Elements: app, lem, and rdg

questiontext.text: In the TEI textcrit module, how are the atomic components of a variation unit structured within an apparatus entry?

generalfeedback.text: An container encloses the variation unit, using for the preferred reading and for variant alternatives.

answer.text: An element encapsulates the variation unit, containing an optional for the base or preferred reading and one or more elements for variant readings.

feedback.text: Correct. The container wraps the variation locus, using for the lemma and for competing variants attested across witnesses.

answer.text: A element acts as the outermost parent container, wrapping nested and tags inside it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. is the parent container for the variation unit; and are child elements inside .

answer.text: An element must contain at least two elements to represent competing editorial choices.

feedback.text: Incorrect. An may contain zero or one ; competing variants are encoded in multiple elements.

answer.text: The element contains editorial metadata, while the element stores the list of manuscript shelfmarks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Both and contain textual readings, with witness metadata recorded in attributes like @wit.

name.text: 06 Question: Witness Sigla and the wit Attribute

questiontext.text: How does the @wit attribute in TEI XML establish referential integrity between apparatus readings and manuscript witnesses?

generalfeedback.text: The @wit attribute uses space-separated #sigla pointers to link readings directly to authoritative manuscript identifiers declared in the TEI Header.

answer.text: It contains a whitespace-separated list of private URI pointers (e.g. wit="#CodexA #CodexB") targeting unique xml:id values declared in the witness list.

feedback.text: Correct. Each token in @wit is an IDREF prefixed with '#' pointing to a specific declared in the document header.

answer.text: It stores a free-text citation giving the shelfmark and city of the manuscript in plain prose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Shelfmarks and repository data belong in metadata; @wit uses compact IDREF URI pointers.

answer.text: It uses comma-separated integers representing the chronological date of each manuscript.

feedback.text: Incorrect. @wit contains space-separated URI pointers to witness identifiers, not dates.

answer.text: It is an optional boolean flag indicating whether the reading was witnessed by the primary editor.

feedback.text: Incorrect. @wit explicitly identifies the historical witnesses (manuscripts, papyri, print editions) supporting the reading.

name.text: 07 Question: Documenting the Witnesses: listWit and witness

questiontext.text: Where are manuscript sigla formally declared in a TEI critical edition, and how can witness groups be represented?

generalfeedback.text: The element in the TEI Header defines authoritative @xml:id identifiers, nested families, and metadata for every manuscript cited in the edition.

answer.text: Inside in the or front matter, where individual elements define unique @xml:id attributes and nested elements group manuscript families.

feedback.text: Correct. The element defines authoritative manuscript metadata and can be nested to assign group sigla to entire manuscript families.

answer.text: Inside the text as inline comments before each paragraph.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Witness declarations belong in structured metadata (), not in informal body comments.

answer.text: In an external CSS stylesheet linked to the HTML output page.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Stylesheets control presentation, not the semantic declaration and validation of manuscript witnesses.

answer.text: Within each element as child tags repeated at every variation unit.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Manuscript descriptions are declared once centrally in and referenced via @wit pointers to avoid massive redundancy.

name.text: 08 Question: Nested and Hierarchical Variants: rdgGrp

questiontext.text: What is the primary advantage of using the element within an variation unit?

generalfeedback.text: The element structures complex variations hierarchically, grouping minor orthographic sub-variants beneath major lexical or stemmatic divergences.

answer.text: It allows editors to organize complex variants hierarchically, grouping minor orthographic sub-variants under major substantive or stemmatic branches.

feedback.text: Correct. prevents variation flattening, allowing algorithms to analyze major lexical divergences while clustering itacisms or spelling corruptions beneath them.

answer.text: It automatically generates digital facsimiles of the grouped manuscripts from online digital libraries.

feedback.text: Incorrect. structures textual data in XML; it does not fetch image facsimiles.

answer.text: It forces all grouped witnesses to be treated as a single unified manuscript in the .

feedback.text: Incorrect. Grouped readings retain individual witness citations via @wit on their child tags.

answer.text: It deletes non-substantive readings from the XML file during schema validation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. preserves sub-variants within a structured hierarchy rather than deleting them.

name.text: 09 Question: Codicological and Paleographical Context: witDetail

questiontext.text: How does the element enrich a critical apparatus entry in TEI XML?

generalfeedback.text: The element captures essential paleographical and codicological context—such as erasures, corrections, and marginal additions—tied directly to specific witness readings.

answer.text: It records specific paleographical, codicological, or physical details about a reading (such as erasures or corrections) linked via @wit and @target.

feedback.text: Correct. captures physical manuscript context—such as text written in rasura or added in margins—tied directly to specific witness readings.

answer.text: It translates the Greek or Latin reading into modern vernacular prose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Translations are encoded in or , whereas records codicological and paleographical notes.

answer.text: It computes the statistical probability that a scribal reading is authentic.

feedback.text: Incorrect. provides descriptive physical context, not statistical authenticity calculations.

answer.text: It replaces the declaration in the .

feedback.text: Incorrect. annotates specific apparatus readings in the text, while defines repository metadata in the header.

name.text: 10 Question: Handling Physical Damage: lacunaStart and lacunaEnd

questiontext.text: Why are milestone elements and essential in computational textual criticism?

generalfeedback.text: Milestone elements and explicitly define spans of physical destruction, preventing algorithms from misclassifying physical loss as intentional omission.

answer.text: They explicitly delimit spans of physical damage for specific witnesses, preventing collation algorithms from treating physical loss as intentional scribal omission.

feedback.text: Correct. Milestone lacuna tags maintain an accurate state of witness availability, ensuring damaged witnesses are not penalized as omissions or falsely scored as agreeing with the lemma.

answer.text: They automatically reconstruct the destroyed text using neural language models.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Conjectural reconstructions are tagged with , while lacuna milestones mark physical absence.

answer.text: They instruct the XML parser to skip schema validation for damaged sections.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Lacuna milestones are fully valid TEI elements and do not disable validation.

answer.text: They convert positive apparatus entries into negative apparatus entries dynamically.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Lacuna tags explicitly document physical gaps regardless of whether the presentation is positive or negative.

name.text: 11 Question: The OHCO Problem in Textual Criticism

questiontext.text: What is the Ordered Hierarchy of Content Objects (OHCO) problem when encoding critical apparatuses in XML?

generalfeedback.text: The OHCO model of XML forbids overlapping tags, requiring specialized TEI linking architectures to handle variants that cross structural boundaries.

answer.text: XML enforces strict tree nesting without tag overlap, making it impossible for inline elements to naturally cross structural boundaries like sentences, verses, or lines.

feedback.text: Correct. Textual variation in manuscripts frequently crosses structural XML boundaries (e.g. spanning two sentences or verse lines), causing overlapping tag errors in basic XML trees.

answer.text: XML files cannot store non-Latin character sets such as Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic.

feedback.text: Incorrect. XML supports full Unicode (UTF-8); the OHCO problem is strictly an architectural limitation regarding overlapping hierarchical trees.

answer.text: Collation software cannot process files larger than a single paragraph.

feedback.text: Incorrect. File size is not the issue; the constraint is XML's syntactic prohibition against overlapping elements.

answer.text: Manuscript sigla must be sorted in strict alphabetical order within the .

feedback.text: Incorrect. Sigla ordering is an editorial choice, not related to the OHCO hierarchical overlap problem.

name.text: 12 Question: Declaration of Linking Method: variantEncoding

questiontext.text: What is the purpose of the element in the TEI Header's ?

generalfeedback.text: The element in the TEI Header declares the project's chosen apparatus architecture (method and location) for all downstream software tools.

answer.text: It formally declares the apparatus linking architecture by specifying the linking method (@method) and storage location (@location) for processing tools.

feedback.text: Correct. specifies whether the edition uses parallel-segmentation, location-referenced, or double-endpoint-attachment, and whether apparatus entries are internal or external.

answer.text: It defines the font encodings and character glyph tables used in the PDF edition.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Typography and font settings belong to publishing stylesheets, not .

answer.text: It lists all known scribal hands and ink formulations across the collated manuscripts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Scribal hands are defined in inside .

answer.text: It sets the access permissions and open-access licensing terms for the digital edition.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Licensing information is declared in via .

name.text: 13 Question: Method 1: Parallel Segmentation

questiontext.text: What characterizes the Parallel Segmentation method in TEI critical apparatus encoding?

generalfeedback.text: Parallel segmentation embeds directly inline, making it ideal for XSLT transformation and automated collation, but unable to handle overlapping hierarchies.

answer.text: The element is embedded directly inline in the text stream, with invariant text surrounding it and variant readings enclosed in and tags.

feedback.text: Correct. In parallel segmentation, the apparatus is the text: variation units are inline, making XSLT transformation and CollateX export straightforward, though overlapping hierarchies are unsupported.

answer.text: Apparatus entries are stored in a separate database and referenced only by line numbers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That describes the location-referenced method; parallel segmentation embeds directly inline.

answer.text: All variant readings are stripped from the main XML file and published in an appendix.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Parallel segmentation keeps all readings inline within the main text flow.

answer.text: It requires every manuscript to be encoded as an independent, standalone XML file.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Parallel segmentation merges multi-witness variation into a single inline TEI stream.

name.text: 14 Question: Drafting Parallel Segmentation by Hand

questiontext.text: When drafting a parallel segmentation apparatus by hand, how are textual additions and omissions explicitly encoded?

generalfeedback.text: In parallel segmentation, omissions and additions are explicitly encoded using empty or tags embedded directly within the inline token stream.

answer.text: Additions and omissions are represented using empty or tags for witnesses where the text is absent, paired with populated tags for witnesses where it is present.

feedback.text: Correct. An empty or explicitly marks the absence of text in specific witnesses while maintaining positive attestation across the inline token stream.

answer.text: Omissions are silently deleted from the file without leaving any tag in the apparatus.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Silently omitting witnesses converts the entry into an ambiguous negative record; an empty element explicitly records the omission.

answer.text: Additions must be encoded as external footnotes using the element.

feedback.text: Incorrect. In parallel segmentation, additions are encoded directly inside as elements containing the added text.

answer.text: The entire paragraph must be duplicated for each witness that contains an omission.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Duplicating paragraphs defeats the purpose of inline parallel segmentation; only the divergent token span is enclosed in .

name.text: 15 Question: Method 2: Location-Referenced

questiontext.text: What is the chief operational limitation of the Location-Referenced apparatus method in digital editing?

generalfeedback.text: Location-referenced apparatuses cleanly separate base text from variants using @loc coordinates, but their informal linkage makes automated computational processing exceedingly difficult.

answer.text: Its informal @loc coordinates (e.g. loc="line 14") make it extremely difficult for automated software to determine exact word boundaries or dynamically reconstruct witnesses.

feedback.text: Correct. Location-referenced apparatuses cleanly separate base text from variants, but informal coordinates prevent exact computational alignment and algorithmic witness reconstruction.

answer.text: It cannot be validated against any TEI P5 Relax NG schema.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The location-referenced method is fully standard and valid in TEI P5 Chapter 13.

answer.text: It requires all manuscript images to be embedded directly inside the XML body.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Image facsimiles are linked via standard URIs and are independent of the apparatus linking method.

answer.text: It is impossible for human classicists to read in print layouts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Location-referenced apparatuses directly mimic traditional print layouts, making them easy for humans to read but hard for algorithms to parse.

name.text: 16 Question: Drafting Location-Referenced Apparatus by Hand

questiontext.text: Why is an explicit element mandatory in every entry of a location-referenced apparatus?

generalfeedback.text: Location-referenced apparatuses require explicit lemmas to identify the target phrase within the referenced line or verse coordinate.

answer.text: Because the external apparatus entry must quote the specific target phrase in the referenced line to identify which words are subject to variation.

feedback.text: Correct. Since the apparatus is stored externally and linked only by line or verse number, the lemma is required to identify the exact contested words in that line.

answer.text: Because TEI schemas reject any XML document that contains without a .

feedback.text: Incorrect. TEI allows un-lemmatized in parallel segmentation; the requirement in location-referenced encoding is functional and disambiguating.

answer.text: Because the lemma determines the font size of the footnote in print output.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Styling is controlled by stylesheets, not by element semantics.

answer.text: Because witness sigla can only be attached to tags in this method.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Witness sigla are attached to both and elements via @wit.

name.text: 17 Question: Method 3: Double-Endpoint Attachment

questiontext.text: How does the Double-Endpoint Attachment method resolve the OHCO overlapping hierarchy problem in TEI apparatus encoding?

generalfeedback.text: Double-endpoint attachment uses external elements pointing to milestones via @from and @to, solving overlapping hierarchies with exact computational precision.

answer.text: It places empty milestones with unique IDs in the base text and links external entries to exact start and end spans via @from and @to attributes.

feedback.text: Correct. Because milestones are empty, they can sit anywhere across structural boundaries, while external entries reference their exact IDs via @from and @to.

answer.text: It stores each word in an external SQL database and queries it via HTTP requests.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Double-endpoint attachment is a native TEI XML structure using and , not a SQL database requirement.

answer.text: It duplicates the entire text stream for every combination of overlapping tags.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Double-endpoint attachment maintains a single base text with milestone anchors, avoiding text duplication.

answer.text: It disables XML schema validation to allow overlapping start and end tags in the body.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Double-endpoint attachment maintains strict XML well-formedness and schema validity by using empty milestone elements.

name.text: 18 Question: Drafting Double-Endpoint Attachment by Hand

questiontext.text: What practical overhead does an editor encounter when drafting double-endpoint attachment markup by hand?

generalfeedback.text: Double-endpoint attachment easily spans structural tags like line and stanza boundaries, but demands meticulous maintenance of anchor identifiers.

answer.text: The editor must invent, insert, and meticulously maintain unique anchor IDs across the entire text, ensuring every @from and @to pointer resolves correctly.

feedback.text: Correct. Double-endpoint attachment provides total structural flexibility across boundaries, but requires high manual overhead to manage hundreds of anchor identifiers.

answer.text: The editor must translate all manuscript readings into Classical Latin before encoding.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Double-endpoint attachment works in any language and does not require translation.

answer.text: The editor is prohibited from recording more than one variant reading per chapter.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Any number of elements can be attached to a double-endpoint entry.

answer.text: The editor cannot include witness sigla in external apparatus entries.

feedback.text: Incorrect. External apparatus entries in double-endpoint attachment use standard @wit attributes on and .

name.text: 19 Question: Comparing the Three TEI Linking Methods

questiontext.text: Which pair correctly matches the TEI apparatus linking method with its primary practical strength?

generalfeedback.text: Choose Parallel Segmentation for automated collation workflows, and Double-Endpoint Attachment when managing overlapping structural hierarchies and complex transpositions.

answer.text: Parallel Segmentation provides seamless compatibility with automated collation tools, while Double-Endpoint Attachment fully supports overlapping structural hierarchies.

feedback.text: Correct. CollateX natively exports parallel segmentation, while double-endpoint attachment solves overlapping structures like verse lines and transpositions.

answer.text: Location-Referenced enables exact algorithmic witness reconstruction, while Parallel Segmentation is used only for print.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Location-referenced makes algorithmic reconstruction difficult; parallel segmentation is the primary digital format.

answer.text: Double-Endpoint Attachment eliminates the need for manuscript sigla, while Location-Referenced requires no base text.

feedback.text: Incorrect. All methods require sigla, and location-referenced relies heavily on a base text.

answer.text: Parallel Segmentation is restricted to single-witness editions, while Double-Endpoint Attachment is restricted to modern poetry.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Both methods support multi-witness traditions across all historical genres.

name.text: 20 Question: Editorial Judgement and Lemma Selection

questiontext.text: In critical editing, what theoretical commitment is reflected when choosing what reading to place in the element versus an element?

generalfeedback.text: The element embodies editorial judgement—whether designating a historical copy-text reading or an eclectically reconstructed original.

answer.text: Designating a copy-text places historical readings of a single witness in , whereas an eclectic edition places an editorially reconstructed archetype in .

feedback.text: Correct. The reflects editorial theory: in copy-text editing it represents a specific physical document, while in eclectic editing it represents a critically reconstructed reading.

answer.text: The must always be the reading found in the latest printed edition.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Textual critics prioritize early manuscript evidence or reconstructed archetypes, not modern reprints.

answer.text: The is automatically assigned by XML schema validators based on word length.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Lemma selection is a critical philological decision, not an automated schema function.

answer.text: An editor is prohibited from recording personal conjectures or emendations in the element.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Editorial conjectures can be placed in , documented transparently using the @resp attribute.

name.text: 21 Question: Typology of Readings: The type and cause Attributes

questiontext.text: How do the @type and @cause attributes on transform a critical apparatus into a dataset for historical linguistics and scribal studies?

generalfeedback.text: Use @type to classify the linguistic category of a variant and @cause to record the paleographical mechanism behind the scribal divergence.

answer.text: @type classifies the linguistic category (e.g. substantive, orthographic, transposition), while @cause records the paleographical or psychological mechanism (e.g. homoioteleuton, itacism).

feedback.text: Correct. Explicit taxonomy allows scholars to filter out phonetic noise, analyze scribal copying habits, and trace dialectal evolution across centuries.

answer.text: They record the physical dimensions and parchment thickness of the manuscript folios.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Physical manuscript dimensions belong in in the header, not in apparatus attributes.

answer.text: They automatically delete ungrammatical readings from the published edition.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Textual criticism preserves ungrammatical readings as crucial evidence of transmission.

answer.text: They assign legal copyright licenses to individual scribal variations.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Ancient and medieval manuscript readings are public domain; attributes describe linguistic and paleographical properties.

name.text: 22 Question: Scribal Hands and Layers: hand and add / del

questiontext.text: How does TEI XML distinguish between an original scribe's reading and subsequent corrections made by later hands in the same manuscript?

generalfeedback.text: The @hand attribute and embedded / elements precisely record multi-layered scribal corrections across different historical hands within a single witness.

answer.text: By combining the manuscript's @wit siglum with the @hand attribute (targeting declared IDs) and embedding genetic tags like , , or .

feedback.text: Correct. Combining @wit with @hand (e.g. wit="#SinaitGr" hand="#Sinait_corr") and tags like / documents multi-layered corrections within a single witness.

answer.text: By creating a completely new manuscript shelfmark in the for every scribal correction.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The physical manuscript retains its unique identifier, with hands distinguished via @hand and .

answer.text: By converting the original reading into an external footnote and overwriting the XML text.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Digital editing preserves all historical layers in structured markup rather than overwriting text.

answer.text: By deleting the corrector's reading if it disagrees with the primary editor's preference.

feedback.text: Incorrect. An apparatus records historical evidence objectively, including all identifiable correction layers.

name.text: 23 Question: Case Study: St. Francis Xavier University Special Collections

questiontext.text: What do the Gaelic manuscripts in the StFX Special Collections illustrate about the necessity of positive digital apparatus encoding?

generalfeedback.text: Physical archival holdings—such as StFX's Gaelic manuscripts—demonstrate that positive digital apparatus encoding is essential for capturing dialectal and performance variance without editorial distortion.

answer.text: In fluid oral-formulaic traditions with non-standardized orthography, positive apparatus encoding preserves authentic dialectal, performance, and regional variants without editorial flattening.

feedback.text: Correct. The Ridge Manuscripts and Nova Scotian Gaelic poetry exhibit extreme orthographic and performance fluidity that a rigid print negative apparatus would obscure.

answer.text: Gaelic poetry can only be collated using proprietary closed-source software.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Standard open-source TEI XML and CollateX tools handle Gaelic poetry effectively.

answer.text: Oral poetry contains zero textual variation because bards memorized texts perfectly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Oral and manuscript transmission produced widespread lexical, phonological, and structural variations.

answer.text: Eighteenth-century Scottish Gaelic manuscripts conform strictly to Lachmannian stemma rules.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Oral-formulaic and regional traditions involve horizontal transmission and performance variance that resist rigid Lachmannian family trees.

name.text: 24 Question: Case Study: The Homer Multitext (HMT) and Venetus A

questiontext.text: Why did the Homer Multitext project reject traditional Lachmannian base-text apparatuses in favor of a multi-text digital architecture?

generalfeedback.text: The Homer Multitext proves that print apparatuses frequently suppress vital physical evidence, demonstrating the need for multi-text digital architectures.

answer.text: Because Homeric epic evolved through oral-formulaic performance without a single original autograph, and print apparatuses suppressed crucial physical data like scholia and erasures.

feedback.text: Correct. The HMT treats every manuscript (such as Venetus A) as an autonomous performance witness, using CTS URNs and stand-off markup to represent text, scholia, and physical images equally.

answer.text: Because the Iliad was written in Latin and could not be encoded in Greek TEI XML.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The Iliad is in ancient Greek and is richly encoded in TEI XML within the HMT project.

answer.text: Because digital editions are prohibited from citing manuscripts earlier than the tenth century.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The HMT specifically centers on the 10th-century Venetus A codex and earlier papyri.

answer.text: Because print apparatuses were found to contain zero typographical abbreviations.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Print apparatuses were densely abbreviated, which often concealed vital physical and contextual evidence.

name.text: 25 Question: Case Study: Editio Critica Maior (ECM) of the Greek New Testament

questiontext.text: How does the Editio Critica Maior (ECM) utilize exhaustive TEI apparatus encoding to solve the problem of contaminated manuscript traditions?

generalfeedback.text: The ECM demonstrates how exhaustive TEI apparatus encoding provides the mathematical dataset required for modern phylogenetic methods like the CBGM.

answer.text: Every variation unit is encoded with full positive attestation in TEI XML, providing the machine-readable dataset required for the Coherence-Based Genealogical Method (CBGM).

feedback.text: Correct. The CBGM calculates statistical coherence and pre-genealogical flow across thousands of variation units, which requires exhaustively validated positive TEI apparatus data.

answer.text: The ECM uses machine learning to automatically delete 90% of surviving New Testament manuscripts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The ECM collates hundreds of intensive Greek witnesses without deleting manuscript evidence.

answer.text: The ECM replaces all Greek manuscript evidence with Latin Vulgate readings.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The ECM focuses on reconstructing the Ausgangstext (Initial Text) of the Greek New Testament.

answer.text: The ECM relies exclusively on negative apparatus footnotes to minimize computer file sizes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The ECM requires comprehensive positive apparatus datasets to feed its mathematical algorithms.

name.text: 26 Question: Manual Encoding Exercises: The Three Passages

questiontext.text: What critical editorial discipline is reinforced when manually encoding complex multi-word transpositions and physical lacunae?

generalfeedback.text: Manual encoding of multi-word variants and lacunae forces the editor to define precise variation unit boundaries and handle physical damage explicitly.

answer.text: The editor is forced to explicitly define variation unit boundaries, account for every active witness, and distinguish physical absence from intentional omission.

feedback.text: Correct. Manual encoding reveals the exact boundaries of variation units, forces positive accountability across witnesses, and ensures lacunae are not mistaken for omissions.

answer.text: The editor learns to let automated software make all lemma and boundary decisions.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Manual exercises train human editorial judgement, which serves as the ground truth for evaluating software.

answer.text: The editor is trained to discard damaged manuscripts rather than encoding lacuna milestones.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The exercise explicitly trains editors to encode lacuna milestones (/).

answer.text: The editor memorizes standard XML tags so that schema validation can be bypassed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schema validation is a mandatory quality gate, not something to be bypassed.

name.text: 27 Question: Common Syntax Pitfalls in Manual TEI XML

questiontext.text: Which of the following represents a fatal syntax error that prevents a TEI critical apparatus file from validating?

generalfeedback.text: Strict vigilance over IDREF pointers, URI # prefixes, XML entity escaping, and milestone closure prevents fatal validation failures in hand-crafted TEI.

answer.text: Using a bare ampersand (&) instead of &, or omitting the '#' prefix in a @wit attribute value.

feedback.text: Correct. Bare ampersands violate XML well-formedness, and omitting the '#' prefix creates an invalid URI reference in @wit IDREF validation.

answer.text: Nesting an element inside an container.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Nesting inside is standard, valid TEI syntax.

answer.text: Including Greek Unicode characters in the text content of a element.

feedback.text: Incorrect. TEI XML natively supports all Unicode scripts and characters.

answer.text: Declaring manuscript identifiers with unique xml:id values in the .

feedback.text: Incorrect. Declaring unique xml:id attributes in is required for referential integrity.

name.text: 28 Question: Building the Method Reference Document

questiontext.text: What is the primary function of a Method Reference Document in a collaborative digital critical edition?

generalfeedback.text: A Method Reference Document formalizes project rules for linking methods, lemma selection, variant classification, and witness sigla.

answer.text: To establish a binding editorial constitution defining project rules for linking methods, lemma selection, variant classification taxonomies, and sigla authority.
